name: Focus Kit
description: A data-only focus toolkit for DSH Mobile: a docked Focus page with a 25-minute on-screen timer, a three-step start ritual, prompts you can copy into chat, and a details page that explains exactly what is and is not running. Nothing runs in the background: the timer is local to the page, the copy actions write to the clipboard, and every button is one fixed action the app already knows. Ships a Focus Amber accent derived from the bundled Refined Ember palette.
author: DSH Mobile Samples

body.title: Focus Kit
body.intro: Twenty-five minutes, one outcome. Set the timer, run the three-step ritual, and copy a prompt into chat when you want the assistant to hold you to the block.

components.text: Pick one outcome, start the clock

Choose the outcome before the timer starts. If you cannot name it in one sentence, the first block is deciding what the outcome is, and that still counts. The timer lives on this page only, so use it while you are here and copy the prompt when you want the assistant to keep the block honest.

components.label: Focus block
components.note: Local to this page. Leaving resets it; nothing buzzes.

items.label: Name the outcome in one sentence
items.note: Finishable inside the block, and worth finishing.

items.label: Silence the phone
items.note: Do Not Disturb on; face down if the screen pulls at you.

items.label: Open the file, ticket or session you will touch
items.note: The block starts with the thing already on screen.

components.title: If the block stalls
components.text: Stalled is data, not failure. Copy the stall prompt, say what you are avoiding, and let the assistant shrink the next step until it is startable. A block that ends in a smaller next step still worked.
A block you can start is worth more than a plan you cannot. Make the next action small enough to be embarrassing.

actions.label: COPY FOCUS PROMPT
actions.value: I have one 25-minute focus block and one outcome: <name it here>. First ask me for the outcome in one sentence. Then give me only the first concrete step and stop - no plan, no alternatives. If that step takes more than 10 minutes, cut it in half. When I say the block is done, ask what actually finished and help me write one line of evidence.

body.title: How Focus Kit works
body.intro: The page above is declarative JSON rendered by the app. This page is the honest fine print: what the timer does, why it cannot buzz, and how to update the file.

sections.title: How it works
sections.text: The countdown is a widget in the page renderer. It starts when you tap start, ticks while the page is open, and resets when you leave. The pack itself stores nothing: no timer, no state, no event history.

sections.title: Why no background timer
sections.text: A declarative pack is data, never code, so it cannot start a foreground service, schedule an alarm or post a notification. A pack that promised to buzz mid-block would be lying. Use the on-screen clock while you work, and the copied prompt as the part that survives leaving the page.

sections.title: How to update it
sections.text: Settings -> Plugins -> check for updates on this pack, or reinstall from the repository. The repository's dsh-plugin.json is this exact file; only version and content change between releases.

sections.title: How to make it yours
sections.text: Fork github.com/James0507-cell/dsh-plugin-focus-timer, edit the prompt in the copy action and the block lengths, bump version, push, then point the installer at your fork. The app validates the whole file before installing it.

items.text: Timer and checklist state live in the renderer
items.note: Leaving the page resets them; the pack writes nothing to disk.

items.text: Copy actions write to the clipboard only
items.note: The app confirms with a toast; the text is not sent anywhere.

items.text: The page makes no network calls
items.note: The plugin manager fetches updates, not the page.
